//: Rate card, Everyday Card balance transfer (product 20). Owner: Treasury.
//1: THIS IS THE CARD THAT BREAKS THE SCALAR ASSUMPTION. A cell holds two rates and
//2: a duration. There is no sensible scalar for `.at(...)` to return here, which is
//3: why the lookup returns a declared ROW and the step names the fields it reads.
//4: See FRAMEWORK-DEMANDS D5. Doc 03's provisional Table sketch returns
//5: `tables.term.max_loan[term]` - a scalar - and that assumption is wrong.

promotional.//: 12 grades x 8 limit bands x 5 promotional durations = 480 cells. Sample.

reversion.//: 12 grades x 20 limit bands = 240 cells. The rate that actually decides the
reversion.//1: total cost, and the rate CON-INT-06 is evaluated against. Sample.

mechanics.transfer_fee_note: Added to the utilised balance, not paid in cash, which means it accrues at the promotional rate and then at the reversion rate. It is part of total_cost_of_credit.
mechanics.max_transferred_note: So the client is not immediately at the ceiling.
mechanics.minimum_payment_formula: max(floor, pct% of balance + interest + fees)
mechanics.mandatory_paydown_note: 1/36 of the transferred amount per month, contractual, IN ADDITION to the minimum payment, so the transferred balance amortises within 36 months. Without this a balance transfer is an indefinite extension at a reverted rate and the anti-harm rule has nothing to measure.
mechanics.affordability_note: NOT the promotional minimum payment. Affordability is tested against the reversion rate applied to the FULL APPROVED LIMIT, amortised over 36 months. A client who can afford the R310 promotional minimum but not the R1 240 stressed payment has been sold a cliff.
mechanics.total_cost_note: Not at the promotional rate throughout, which is how this product is mis-sold.
